title: GIC and Saudi Telecom compete on Pure DC minority stake bid
html:
Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC and Saudi Telecom Company are reportedly bidding for a stake in UK-based Pure Data Centres (Pure DC).

Bloomberg reports that Pure DC owner Oaktree Capital Management was looking to bring in a minority investor to fund the developer’s expansion.

The report said GIC had joined with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) for its bid.

According to Bloomberg’s sources, Oaktree is seeking an $8 billion valuation for Pure DC. DCD has reached out to the involved parties for confirmation and further information.

Earlier this month, Pure DC secured $1.9 billion in new financing to support its data center buildout. The latest announcement puts the company’s year-to-date secured financing at more than $6bn.

Backed by Oaktree, Pure DC claims to have more than 1GW of IT capacity in operation or development across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. The company aims to triple this capacity and position itself as a leader in data centers in Europe and the Middle East.

GIC was established by the government of Singapore in 1981. It has invested in a range of data center operations in recent years, including Vantage’s EMEA data center platform, multiple Equinix xScale hyperscale data centers, US firm EdgeCore, and Czech digital infrastructure firm CETIN Group.

In August, GIC and Macquarie Asset Management formed a strategic partnership with Anthropic to develop, operate, and lease data center infrastructure at scale to Anthropic.

Saudi Telecom Company is a Saudi state-owned telecoms company. It is actively expanding its presence in the Middle East and North Africa and has 25 data centers operational and under construction.
summary: Oaktree seeking $8 billion valuation for Pure DC
